adminIncrementRequest.adminOperationId: A caller-created, opaque, bounded, high-entropy UUIDv4/128-bit-equivalent string identifying exactly one logical ADMIN mutation. It is created before first transmission and reused verbatim for exact retries. It is neither a credential nor an actor identity and never affects authentication or authorization.
adminIncrementRequest.expectedStopEpoch: The caller's observed current epoch and the compare-and-set precondition for the increment.

adminOperationJournal.durability: Persistent and authoritative; never implemented as an in-memory retry cache.
adminOperationJournal.location: The same privileged SQLite transactional store as stopEpoch and audit state.

authorizationGrantIssuance.epochRule: A grant whose stopEpochAtIssuance is less than the current global stopEpoch is void.
authorizationGrantIssuance.identityRule: authenticatedApproverUid comes only from SO_PEERCRED. Free-text approver identity cannot authorize. Claude and Codex model identities never become privileged approver identities and never hold ADMIN capability or credentials.
authorizationGrantIssuance.issuer: Only authledgerd may issue an R3 AuthorizationGrant, following an ADMIN request from an exact-UID-authorized privileged approver and successful independent validation against the trusted CouncilEpochRegistry and evidence.

concurrencyAndCrashSemantics.semantics: Two concurrent identical X requests cause at most one mutation; serialization and the journal make both callers converge on the same committed result.
Different operation IDs X and Y both carrying expectedStopEpoch N cause at most one commit of N+1; the other fails STALE_EXPECTED_STOP_EPOCH, with no N+2.
A crash before COMMIT commits none of the epoch write, journal entry or audit event.
A crash after COMMIT but before ACK leaves epoch, journal and audit durable; an exact retry returns the stored result.
After restart, the persistent journal and stopEpoch remain authoritative; no in-memory reconstruction is trusted.
After an ambiguous response, the caller must resolve it through exact replay or the bounded result lookup and must never perform a blind second increment.

consumeOnceSemantics.consumeIdentity: A persistent unique consume key exactly binding grantId and AuthorizationEnvelope hash, with the grant's allowedScope, prohibitedEffects and stopEpochAtIssuance revalidated against the authoritative grant and current stopEpoch.
consumeOnceSemantics.crashAfterCommit: Consume state and audit are durable; a retry deterministically returns the stored already-consumed result and cannot consume again.
consumeOnceSemantics.crashBeforeCommit: Neither consume state nor its audit event is committed; a retry may perform the single valid consume.
consumeOnceSemantics.duplicates: The first valid consume may transition the grant to consumed. Duplicate or concurrent consumes serialize on the unique consume key; at most one commits, and all later attempts return the deterministic already-consumed result recorded for that key without authorizing another effect.
consumeOnceSemantics.transaction: Under one privileged SQLite write transaction, validate the grant and current epoch, check the unique consume key, insert the consumed record and append the audit event, then COMMIT atomically.
consumeOnceSemantics.v1cRestriction: The ledger may contain this dormant state and API surface, but no V1C production component is connected to use ALLOW_ONCE for an execution effect.

daemonAndOsIdentity.requirements: Run authledgerd exclusively as the dedicated mihver-ledger OS identity. Models, Publication Broker, Night Runner, Authorization Loop, shells, Git, network tools and provider CLIs never receive this identity, ADMIN credentials, ADMIN descriptors or exact-UID ADMIN authorization. authledgerd alone owns and mutates privileged ledger state and performs no external execution effect.

decision.relationship: Narrow successor to decision-6; preserves its substantive architecture without redesign.

exactIncrementTransaction: Authenticate the ADMIN connection using its kernel-supplied SO_PEERCRED UID.
Authorize that exact UID against the root-owned exact-UID ADMIN allowlist; fail closed if the policy ownership, mode or format is invalid.
Validate operationKind, adminOperationId, expectedStopEpoch and all canonical request constraints, then compute requestHash.
Look up the unique key (authenticatedPeerUid, INCREMENT_STOP_EPOCH, adminOperationId).
If an entry exists and its requestHash differs, roll back and return IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE without mutation and without returning the stored result.
If an entry exists and its requestHash matches, return its previously committed resultStopEpoch and resultCode with no mutation and no second audit mutation event.
Otherwise read the authoritative current stopEpoch.
If expectedStopEpoch differs from current stopEpoch, roll back and return STALE_EXPECTED_STOP_EPOCH with no mutation.
If current stopEpoch equals 9007199254740991, roll back and return STOP_EPOCH_EXHAUSTED with no mutation.
Set next = current stopEpoch + 1 and write stopEpoch = next.
Insert the successful journal result and append the audit mutation event whose actor is the authenticatedPeerUid.
COMMIT the stopEpoch write, journal insert and audit append in one atomic commit boundary.
Return next only after successful COMMIT.

lostAckTraceA.trace: Current stopEpoch is N. ADMIN sends operation X with expectedStopEpoch N. The server atomically commits N+1, X's journal entry and the audit event, but the ACK is lost. The caller retries X with the same authenticated UID, operation kind, adminOperationId and expectedStopEpoch N, producing the same requestHash. The stored requestHash proves it is the exact request; the journal returns the previously committed N+1 with no mutation and no second audit mutation event. The epoch never reaches N+2.

lostAckTraceB.trace: Current stopEpoch is N. Operation X atomically commits N+1, its journal entry and audit event, but the ACK is lost and the caller loses X. The caller creates new logical operation Y while still supplying expectedStopEpoch N. Y has a new adminOperationId, so journal replay does not recognize it; the authoritative epoch is already N+1, so expected-epoch CAS fails with STALE_EXPECTED_STOP_EPOCH. No mutation occurs and the epoch never reaches N+2. Both durable journal replay and expected-epoch CAS are mandatory.

operationResultLookup.rules: Available only on the ADMIN socket, authenticated using the same SO_PEERCRED UID. The lookup key is scoped to that authenticated UID so callers can read only their own operations. It is strictly read-only, cannot mutate stopEpoch or the journal, and grants no additional authority.

privilegedStateStore.durability: SQLite durability settings must make COMMIT the authoritative boundary. State is recovered from the persistent store after restart; no in-memory reconstruction is trusted.
privilegedStateStore.ownership: Owned by mihver-ledger in a directory inaccessible for mutation by model-facing identities; root owns the authorization policy and trust-policy material.

requestHashBinding.rule: The authenticatedPeerUid is taken from SO_PEERCRED, not request text. Reuse of the same unique operation identity with different canonical request content fails closed with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE, performs no mutation and does not return the stored result.

socketSplit.adminSocket: A distinct Unix-domain ADMIN socket exposing only privileged trust-registry mutation, evidence import, grant issuance/revocation where supported, stopEpoch increment and bounded ADMIN reads.
socketSplit.boundary: Socket ownership, mode and group provide REACHABILITY ONLY. Every accepted connection is authenticated from kernel-supplied SO_PEERCRED UID, and each RPC is authorized for that exact UID against a root-owned policy appropriate to its socket and operation.
socketSplit.clientSocket: A distinct Unix-domain CLIENT socket exposing only non-administrative ledger queries and dormant authorization/consume-once API surface. It cannot register Council trust, modify UID policy, import trust anchors, issue R3 grants or mutate stopEpoch.

stopEpochDomain.mutationRules: The normal ADMIN API supports increment only, never decrement or reset. Increment at the maximum fails closed with STOP_EPOCH_EXHAUSTED.
stopEpochDomain.serialization: Canonical JSON number only; no BigInt, unsigned-64 claim, floating-point approximation or wraparound.
stopEpochDomain.storage: SQLite INTEGER with CHECK(stopEpoch >= 0 AND stopEpoch <= 9007199254740991).

trustRegistryAndEvidenceImportBoundary.failure: Malformed, unknown, untrusted, mismatched, replacement or rollback evidence fails closed.
trustRegistryAndEvidenceImportBoundary.import: Canonical evidence import occurs only across the privileged ADMIN boundary. authledgerd independently parses and revalidates all model-writable artifacts rather than trusting caller-supplied hash-shaped strings.
trustRegistryAndEvidenceImportBoundary.registry: A privileged CouncilEpochRegistry whose mutations are ADMIN-only and authorized by exact SO_PEERCRED UID.
requiredValidation: CouncilQuorumProof verification wherever authorization policy requires it
trustRegistryAndEvidenceImportBoundary.trustBinding: Each accepted CouncilConfig is exactly bound to its registered trust anchor and epoch. No model-writable CouncilConfig or other artifact can self-establish trust, silently replace a trust anchor or roll it back.

uidAuthenticationAuthorizationBoundary.authentication: The service obtains the authenticated identity exclusively as the kernel-supplied SO_PEERCRED UID.
uidAuthenticationAuthorizationBoundary.authorization: A root-owned, non-model-writable exact-UID allowlist authorizes each ADMIN operation. Wrong ownership, unsafe mode, malformed content or unknown policy data causes fail-closed startup or request rejection.
uidAuthenticationAuthorizationBoundary.callerText: Caller-supplied uid, actor, approverUid, identity or similar text never overrides or supplements the kernel identity in any RPC.
uidAuthenticationAuthorizationBoundary.reachability: Socket ownership, mode and group are reachability controls only.

v1cExitGate.boundary: Publication Broker remains structurally separate. V1D requires a separate gated decision before any production consumer or execution gateway may exist.

proposalContent.summary: Decision-7 is the narrow successor to decision-6: it preserves the accepted V1C local privilege-separated Authorization Ledger architecture and corrects only the mandatory matrix defect by providing 17 independently represented NO answers.

decisionQuestion: What exact V1C privileged architecture should MIHVER adopt for the Authorization Ledger -- covering the privileged authledgerd daemon and its dedicated OS identity, the ADMIN/CLIENT socket split with SO_PEERCRED kernel peer authentication and exact-UID authorization, the trusted Council/evidence import boundary, exact-bound R3 AuthorizationGrant issuance, consume-once state, and the persistent global stopEpoch register INCLUDING its complete retry-safe, application-level idempotent ADMIN increment protocol -- while preserving strict privilege separation and guaranteeing ZERO execution-effect consumers at V1C exit? This is a NEW candidate (decision-7) and a NARROW SUCCESSOR to decision-6. Decision-6's substantive architecture was sound and MUST be preserved: reproduce it faithfully rather than redesigning it. Decision-6 nevertheless failed R3 quorum for exactly one reason: its mandatory yes/no matrix answered only 15 of the 17 required questions because it collapsed the distinct CLAUDE and CODEX questions into shared entries. V7's sole required material revision is therefore an EXACT 17-of-17 independently represented mandatory yes/no matrix, reproduced verbatim per evidence items 2, 3 and 4 under the structural contract in evidence item 1. Permanently closed candidates that must not be resubmitted, renamed or reused: sha256:9bc6b4c3c63ffa02563d936557bfaced13e6f6251f7c0084bbd3abc01805a063 (V5) and sha256:c5d16bea3806ff0d10b7e092f8d2240d14d68b9461aeb44c206bf7fcb2fafb90 (V6). Your payload must be concrete enough that a fresh implementation team could build it without reopening any trust-boundary decision.
evidence: MANDATORY STRUCTURAL CONTRACT (V7's sole required material revision; this is what V6 failed). payload.yesNoMatrix MUST be a JSON ARRAY of EXACTLY 17 objects, in ascending id order Q01..Q17. Each element MUST have EXACTLY the three fields id, question, answer -- no more, no fewer. id MUST be the exact string Q01..Q17, each used exactly once. question MUST be reproduced BYTE-FOR-BYTE VERBATIM from evidence items 2, 3 and 4. Do not paraphrase, abbreviate, re-case, re-punctuate, or shorten it. answer MUST be exactly the string NO for all 17 entries. You MUST NOT merge, alias, combine or de-duplicate any two questions, MUST NOT answer one question by reference to another, and MUST NOT omit a question because it looks redundant. Q01/Q02, Q03/Q04 and Q08/Q09 are deliberately near-identical CLAUDE vs CODEX pairs: each pair REQUIRES two separate entries. A generic combined Claude/Codex entry is an automatic failure. This matrix is mechanically validated before any vote is requested.

REQUIRED YES/NO MATRIX -- PART 1 OF 3. Reproduce each question string verbatim.
Q01. CAN CLAUDE ISSUE AN R3 AUTHORIZATIONGRANT? ANSWER: NO

BASELINE TO PRESERVE (decision-6's accepted architecture; do not redesign unless you can name a concrete contradiction): dedicated authledgerd daemon; dedicated mihver-ledger OS identity; separate ADMIN and CLIENT Unix-domain sockets; filesystem permissions/ownership/group = REACHABILITY ONLY; SO_PEERCRED UID = authenticated kernel peer identity; root-owned exact-UID allowlist = AUTHORIZATION; privileged SQLite/WAL state; root-owned, non-model-writable admin policy; trusted CouncilEpochRegistry; canonical evidence import with independent revalidation; safe bounded persistent stopEpoch; exact-bound R3 AuthorizationGrant; durable admin operation journal; request-level stopEpoch idempotency; expected-epoch CAS; consume-once authorization state; transactional audit; Publication Broker structurally separate; NO Execution Gateway; zero production consumers of checkAndConsume/ALLOW_ONCE at V1C exit; V1D separately gated.

STOPEPOCH NUMERIC DOMAIN (preserve exactly). The implementable JSON/JS/SQLite-safe domain is 0 <= stopEpoch <= 9007199254740991, i.e. Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER = 2^53 - 1. Storage: SQLite INTEGER with an explicit CHECK enforcing exactly that range. NO BigInt through the current canonical JSON contract (the repository serializer throws on BigInt). NO unsigned-64 claim. NO floating-point approximation. NO wraparound. NO reset and NO decrement in the normal ADMIN API. At the maximum, increment fails closed with STOP_EPOCH_EXHAUSTED.

DURABLE ADMIN OPERATION JOURNAL (preserve). Specify privileged durable idempotency state, not in-memory state. Preferred conceptual table admin_operation_journal binding at minimum: authenticatedPeerUid, operationKind, adminOperationId, requestHash, resultCode, resultStopEpoch, createdAt -- with a uniqueness constraint equivalent to (authenticatedPeerUid, operationKind, adminOperationId). State the unique key explicitly. The journal MUST live in the same privileged transactional store as stopEpoch so that a single transaction covers both.

REQUESTHASH BINDING (preserve). A journal entry must bind the operation identity to the EXACT canonical request. For stopEpoch increment, requestHash MUST bind at least: authenticated peer UID, operation kind, adminOperationId, and expectedStopEpoch. Use a domain-separated deterministic canonical hash and state the domain separator. If the SAME operation identity is presented with DIFFERENT canonical request content, the service MUST fail closed with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE, MUST NOT treat it as a retry, MUST NOT mutate state, and MUST NOT return the stored result.

ADMINOPERATIONID AND EXPECTEDSTOPEPOCH SEMANTICS (preserve). The ADMIN increment request MUST carry exact semantic equivalents of adminOperationId and expectedStopEpoch; if you rename them, state the mapping. adminOperationId: a stable identity for ONE logical ADMIN mutation, created by the caller BEFORE first transmission, an opaque bounded high-entropy string (UUIDv4/128-bit equivalent), reused VERBATIM for retries of the SAME logical operation. It is NOT a credential -- possessing it grants nothing -- and it is NOT an actor identity; it never influences authentication or authorization. expectedStopEpoch: the caller's observed current epoch, used as a compare-and-set precondition.

EXACT INCREMENT TRANSACTION (preserve). Specify semantics equivalent to: authenticate the ADMIN peer via SO_PEERCRED UID; authorize that exact UID against the root-owned allowlist; validate the request; BEGIN IMMEDIATE; look up (authenticatedPeerUid, INCREMENT_STOP_EPOCH, adminOperationId). IF an entry exists: if the stored requestHash differs from the current canonical requestHash, fail IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE; else return the previously committed result with NO mutation and NO second epoch increment. ELSE: read current stopEpoch; if expectedStopEpoch != current, fail STALE_EXPECTED_STOP_EPOCH; if current == 9007199254740991, fail STOP_EPOCH_EXHAUSTED; next = current + 1; write stopEpoch = next; write the journal result; append the audit event; COMMIT; return next. The stopEpoch mutation, the journal write and the audit append MUST share ONE atomic commit boundary.

LOST-ACK TRACE A -- SAME OPERATION ID (your payload MUST state this trace explicitly). Current stopEpoch = N. ADMIN sends operation X with expectedStopEpoch = N. The server commits N+1 plus the journal entry plus the audit event. The ACK is LOST. The caller retries X with the same UID, same operation kind and the same expectedStopEpoch = N, hence the same requestHash. REQUIRED RESULT: the journal recognises the exact request, returns the previously committed N+1, performs NO mutation and NO second audit mutation event, and NEVER reaches N+2. State exactly which stored field makes this true.

LOST-ACK TRACE B -- NEW OPERATION ID AFTER LOST ACK (your payload MUST state this trace explicitly). Same start: current stopEpoch = N, operation X commits N+1, the ACK is LOST, and the caller then LOSES X. The caller issues a NEW logical operation Y still carrying expectedStopEpoch = N. REQUIRED RESULT: Y is a genuinely new logical operation, so the journal does not recognise it, but the privileged current epoch is already N+1, so the expected-epoch check fails with STALE_EXPECTED_STOP_EPOCH, no mutation occurs and the system NEVER reaches N+2. BOTH protections -- journal replay AND expected-epoch CAS -- are MANDATORY; a design with only one of the two is rejected.

CONCURRENCY AND CRASH SEMANTICS (all six MUST be covered explicitly). 1: two concurrent identical X requests -> at most ONE mutation, and both callers converge on the same committed result. 2: two DIFFERENT operation ids X and Y both carrying expectedStopEpoch = N -> at most one commits N+1, the other fails stale; no N+2. 3: crash BEFORE COMMIT -> none of the epoch write, journal entry or audit event is committed. 4: crash AFTER COMMIT but BEFORE the ACK -> epoch, journal and audit are durable and an exact retry returns the stored result. 5: restart -> the journal and stopEpoch remain authoritative; no in-memory reconstruction is trusted. 6: ambiguous response -> the caller must never perform a blind second increment.

OPERATION RESULT LOOKUP (preserve one of two options and say which). OPTION A: a bounded authenticated ADMIN read RPC such as getAdminOperationResult(operationKind, adminOperationId). If you choose A, specify: it uses the same SO_PEERCRED identity, is scoped so a caller may only read its own operations, is strictly read-only, cannot mutate the epoch or journal, and expands no authority. OPTION B: exact replay-only resolution with no read RPC. If you choose B, you MUST explain why replay semantics alone provide complete lost-ack recovery.

ADMIN AUTHENTICATION AND AUTHORIZATION (preserve exactly). Socket ownership, mode and group = REACHABILITY ONLY. SO_PEERCRED UID = AUTHENTICATED IDENTITY, obtained by the service from the kernel. Root-owned exact-UID policy = AUTHORIZATION. Caller-supplied text fields such as uid, actor, approverUid or identity MUST NEVER override the kernel peer identity, in ANY RPC. The audit actor is ALWAYS derived from the authenticated peer UID, never from request text. Fail closed on wrong policy-file ownership, mode or format.

TRUST REGISTRY AND EVIDENCE IMPORT (preserve). Privileged CouncilEpochRegistry; ADMIN-only registry mutation; exact CouncilConfig trust binding; no model-writable artifact may self-establish trust; no silent replacement or rollback of a trust anchor; canonical evidence parsing; DecisionRecord recordHash verification; CouncilQuorumProof verification wherever authorization policy requires it; contextHash binding; repositoryHead binding; decisionRequestId/taskId/candidateHash binding; fail closed on malformed or unknown evidence. Every model-writable artifact is untrusted input to be independently revalidated, never a trusted hash-shaped string supplied by a caller.

R3 AUTHORIZATIONGRANT BINDING (preserve). A grant MUST be exactly bound to at least: grantId; AuthorizationEnvelope hash; DecisionRecord recordHash; candidateHash; decisionRequestId; taskId; contextHash; repositoryHead; allowedScope; prohibitedEffects; stopEpochAtIssuance; authenticatedApproverUid; issuedAt and issuance identity; and expiry/revocation state where supported. NO free-text approver identity may authorize. Claude and Codex model identity MUST NOT become a privileged approver identity. A grant whose bound stopEpoch is older than the current global stopEpoch is void.

CONSUME-ONCE AND THE V1D BOUNDARY (preserve). Retain persistent, replay-resistant consume-once state and specify: the consume identity, the transaction boundary, duplicate/concurrent consume behaviour, crash before commit, crash after commit, and the deterministic replay result. The privileged ledger MAY implement DORMANT consume-once state and API surface. BUT the V1C EXIT GATE is ZERO PRODUCTION CONSUMERS: at V1C exit the Publication Broker does not consume ALLOW_ONCE, Night Runner does not, the Authorization Loop does not; shell, Git, network and provider CLIs have no authorized effect integration; authledgerd itself performs NO external effect; no Execution Gateway is implemented. Do NOT claim zero execution consumers while also describing a live downstream consumption flow.

REQUIRED PAYLOAD CONTENT. Beyond payload.yesNoMatrix, your payload MUST concretely cover, in clearly named fields: the daemon and OS identity; the ADMIN/CLIENT socket split; the privileged state store; the stopEpoch domain; adminOperationId and expectedStopEpoch semantics; the admin operation journal and its unique key; the requestHash binding; the exact increment transaction; lost-ack trace A; lost-ack trace B; the six concurrency/crash cases; the operation-result-lookup choice; the UID authentication/authorization boundary; the trust registry and evidence import boundary; the AuthorizationGrant binding; consume-once semantics; and the zero-production-effect-consumer statement including the absence of an Execution Gateway.

SCOPE AND STYLE LIMITS. Do NOT add HSM, TPM, hypervisor, enclave, air-gap, M-of-N human ceremony, Merkle or sparse-Merkle state, blockchain, remote consensus, distributed database or any additional infrastructure unless you name a concrete threat that simpler local OS-level privilege separation does not adequately mitigate for MIHVER's actual local single-machine model. Claude and Codex MUST never hold ADMIN capability or credentials under any circumstance in your design. This is an architecture decision only: no V1C implementation is authorized. Emit ONLY the JSON object with fields summary and payload. Keep it concise and concrete: no chain-of-thought, no hidden reasoning, no markdown.
